answer: Stop sybils with latency-triangulated proof of presence. The network admits agents through one guarded inlet where three beacons fire a pulse challenge hourly; each agent must answer all three within 40 milliseconds, proving one machine, one place. Step one, beacons timestamp replies; step two, triangulation fixes the location; step three, a mismatch freezes the identity and slashes its 400 POA bond. Faking 10,000 identities needs 10,000 machines in 10,000 places: $6,000,000 in hardware plus $4,000,000 in bonds. Like a jetty that admits one boat at a time, presence cannot be photocopied.
